description: Publication this batch belongs to. Determines which publication must be cited when instances of this batch are used.
Surrogate primary key. Internal, not stable across releases.

Human-readable batch identifier. Unique only in combination with sensitivity_type -- the constraint is UNIQUE (id, sensitivity_type), so the same identifier may recur under a different sensitivity_type. Always carry both. Identifier schemes differ per publication and are described in the publication itself; do not parse them, read the columns.

domain: default, auto, few_robot_depots, many_robot_depots, few_dropoff_points, many_dropoff_points, low_robot_service_time, high_robot_service_time, exact_comparison, low_robot_availability, variable_robot_availability
description: Dimension this batch varies relative to the batch with sensitivity_type = 'default' of the same publication. E.g., prefixes few_/low_ reduce and many_/high_ increase the named quantity. The value 'auto' marks a batch whose design is adopted as a whole from the referenced publication rather than varied along one dimension. 'exact_comparison' marks deliberately small batches used for comparison against an exact method -- it varies instance size rather than a problem dimension. Open set: further values may appear in later releases.

City whose road and sidewalk networks were used as the spatial basis of the batch. NULL for instances generated on a synthetic network. The generator's city catalog, with the geographic anchor and elevation tile per city, is in metadata/generation_parameters/generator.yaml.
Number of trucks available per instance in this batch.

domain: '<total> (<stored in robot hubs>)' e.g. '258 (250)'; or the sentinel 'Infinity'
description: Robot fleet size per instance. Stored as text because it encodes a total amount of robots and an the robot count within the robot hubs, plus the sentinel 'Infinity' for an unlimited fleet. A cast to integer fails on both forms -- parse it; see metadata/description.md, 'Known pitfalls'.
Number of customers per instance in this batch.
Share of regular delivery customers that must be served by the truck rather than by a robot.
Share of return-request customers that must be served by the truck. NULL for batches that do not model return requests.
Share of pickup-request customers that must be served by the truck. NULL for batches that do not model pickup requests.
Share of pickup locations that must be served by the truck. NULL for batches without pickup locations.
Share of regular delivery customers that must be served by a robot. NULL where not modeled separately.
Share of return-request customers that must be served by a robot. NULL for batches that do not model return requests.
Share of pickup-request customers that must be served by a robot. NULL for batches that do not model pickup requests.
Share of pickup locations that must be served by a robot. NULL for batches without pickup locations.
Share of all customers that carry a return request.
Share of all customers that carry a pickup request.
AVERAGE number of customers assigned to each pickup location. Note the type: double precision, NOT integer -- it can take fractional values such as 2.9 or 5.7. 0.
Number of pickup locations per instance. 0 for batches without pickup locations.
Number of robot hubs per instance.
Number of drop-off points per instance, at which robots may be released.
Altitude spread of the generated topography. NULL for batches with flat topography.

For synthetic altitudes it describes the smoothness/volatility of the elevations: higher values produce more frequent and more drastic elevation changes over the same spread. Dimensionless; the column carries no unit comment in the database. NULL for batches with flat topography.

domain: descriptive label, '2000 x 2000 m' or '4000 x 4000 m'
description: Nominal label of the service area, in meters. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY -- the authoritative spatial extent of an instance is given by the coordinates in the raw_data location tables, whose scale is instance-set specific and is NOT meters. Do not parse this column to derive an extent, and do not assume it relates to the coordinate values.

Kind of low-emission or access-restricted zone imposed on the service area. NULL for batches without access restrictions. Where present, affected locations carry a matching zone_restriction value in raw_data.
Share of the service area, or of the customers, covered by low-emission zones -- which of the two depends on the generator mode used.
Number of distinct low-emission zones placed in the service area, i.e., three distinct areas can summarize a 10% LEZ share.
Rule used to place the truck depot within the service area. The generator also offers placement at the origin and at the upper left corner.
TRUE if robots may additionally be released from the truck depot, not only from robot hubs, drop-off points and potential customer sites.
Rule used to determine how many pickup locations an instance receives. NULL for batches without pickup locations.
Rule used to place pickup locations in the service area. NULL for batches without pickup locations.
Rule used to assign customers to pickup locations. NULL for batches without pickup locations.
Rule used to place robot hubs in the service area. 'Equal' distributes them evenly over the area; the generator also offers a random placement. NULL where the batch does not record a rule.

Rule for the initial robot count at each depot. 'Fixed' gives every depot the same count; 'Random' and 'Variable' draw per depot. The realized per-location values are in raw_data.network_locations.initial_robot_availability.
Rule for the robot capacity of each hub. The realized per-location values are in raw_data.network_locations.max_robot_capacity.
Rule used to derive time windows for pickup locations. NULL if pickup locations have no time windows or the batch has none.
Length of pickup location time windows. NULL if not applicable.

Rule used to derive customer time windows. 'Depot Dependent' derives the window from the direct depot-to-customer travel time; NULL means the batch models NO customer time windows -- the corresponding raw_data.customers columns are then NULL and must not be coalesced to 0. Values are capitalized.
Length of customer time windows. NULL if not applicable.

domain: Pickup Location Dependent, Depot Dependent, Location Independent
description: Rule used to derive time windows for pickup-request customers. NULL if not applicable.
Length of pickup-customer time windows. NULL if not applicable.

Interval of the multiplier drawn per customer and applied to the direct depot-to-customer travel time to obtain that customer's deadline. Wider intervals produce looser time windows. Parse it; it is not a numeric column.
Number of instances generated in this batch.
Date the batch was generated.
Human-readable summary of what distinguishes this batch from the default batch of the same publication.
Rule used to place drop-off points in the service area.
